# Pretraining

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](pretraining_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Tactile Manipulation → Pretraining

Dexterous manipulation research whose main contribution is tactile pretraining. Cover tactile-derived representation supervision and joint force–action pretraining. Distinguish model architecture, training-only objectives, deployment tactile inputs, predicted forces versus control targets, and pretraining versus downstream fine-tuning. Classify by the main contribution; execution-time contact correction belongs under tactile Execution Feedback and Action Correction. Do not automatically migrate existing tactile-tagged records.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.4] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-4"></a> | **FACT｜WAM architecture · Joint force–action prediction · Tactile-driven action refinement**<br>[FACT: A Multimodal Force-Action-Track Foundation Model for Human-to-Robot Dexterity](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19155v1)<br>Zhi Cao, Yining Hong, Jiaolong Yang, Yejin Choi, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Huang Huang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `wam` `human-demonstration-pretraining` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `force-feedback` `future-force-prediction` `visual-tracks` `joint-flow-matching` `cascaded-action-refinement` `real-world` | FACT jointly pretrains a video–track–action coarse planner and a force–action refiner on human visual–tactile demonstrations, using fresh tactile feedback during execution to jointly predict future fingertip forces and refine unexecuted actions.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Joint pretraining uses 2,000 hours of human EgoForce data and 100 hours of robot demonstrations; both modules use flow matching. A Wan2.2 video backbone jointly predicts video, tracks and coarse actions from instructions, vision and robot state. The refiner reads coarse actions, cached planner features, current fingertip force and force history, using bidirectional attention to jointly denoise future force and actions. Actions execute at 20 Hz with tactile refreshes at 5 Hz; cached coarse plans and a clamped executed prefix allow refinement of only the unexecuted suffix, without online weight updates. Outputs are bimanual end-effector pose changes and finger-joint targets; predicted force is not a control reference. Ten tasks use two Sharpa Wave hands, with an additional 10 robot plus 90 human demonstrations per task for fine-tuning, rather than zero-shot deployment. The project page still labels code and data Coming Soon; downloadable model weights have not been verified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19155v1) · [Project](https://fact-1-0.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-03 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.TACTILE.PRETRAIN.1] <a id="am-man-dex-tactile-pretrain-1"></a> | **Spark-0｜VLA architecture · Tactile supervision of VLM · Tactile input to action expert**<br>[Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.22342v1)<br>Tianxing Chen, Wenwei Lin, Chuqiao Lyu, Peicheng Xiang, Junyuan Tang, Tian Nian, Zijian Cai, Kehe Ye, Chenze Yu, Wenxuan Zhu, Eric J. Chen, Yan Qin, Yue Chen, Tongyu Wu, Junhao Gong, Kai-Chong Lei, Jiahao Zhang, Kailun Su, Qiwei Liang, Renjing Xu, Ping Luo, Wenbo Ding<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `vtla` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `pretraining` `tactile-supervised-visual-pretraining` `contact-map-supervision` `geometry-distillation` `flow-matching` `action-expert` `regional-force-history` `3d-taxels` `tactile-adaln-conditioning` `missing-modality-placeholder` `human-demonstrations` `human-to-robot-transfer` `supervised-fine-tuning` `wuji-hand-2` `simulation` `real-world` | Spark-0 supervises VLM visual representations with tactile-derived contact maps and feeds force histories and 3D taxels to a flow-matching action expert, enabling the pretrained model to support both vision-only and tactile-conditioned dexterous control.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The VLA pairs Qwen3-VL-4B with a 36-layer flow-matching action expert. Glove contacts are mapped onto a human-hand mesh and rendered as head-view contact maps; these targets and a frozen Depth-Anything-3 geometry teacher supervise VLM layer-25 visual tokens. Raw touch never enters the VLM; teacher/alignment heads are removed at inference. Separately, 20-frame regional force histories and current 3D taxels yield 12 force plus 12 spatial tactile tokens, conditioning the action expert through joint attention and force-conditioned AdaLN. AE means Action Expert, not autoencoder. Images, instructions and three state frames condition a 50-row chunk of 58-dimensional bimanual relative end-effector poses and finger-joint targets. Missing touch uses learned placeholders; deployment does not update weights online. HumanTouch contains 1,000 hours across 100+ tasks and 32 operators; each glove uses 320 of 460 taxels after masking 140 flexion-region points. Mixed human/robot/simulation pretraining is followed by benchmark-specific fine-tuning, not zero-shot deployment. SparkArena-Sim has seven vision-only tasks with 50 trials each; SparkArena-Real has five tactile-conditioned tasks with ten paired-initial-state trials each, on the same Gen 1 Prototype with two WUJI Hand 2 hands. With identical RGB and pretraining compute, retaining touch raises vision-only Ego Humanoid success from 52.45% to 71.72% and Real from 44% to 52%. This compares overall tactile pretraining, not an isolated alignment-head or online-touch ablation. Official code and pretrained-checkpoint links are public; complete HumanTouch data and simulator-asset downloads remain unverified, and the project still marks SparkArena-Sim code Coming soon. Dataset and benchmark contributions remain in this single paper record. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.22342v1) · [Project](https://xsparkai.com/Spark-0/) · [Code](https://github.com/XsparkAI/Spark-0) · [Assets](https://huggingface.co/TianxingChen/Spark-0) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-03 |
